newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares staged an impressive comeback on Friday, recouping much of the hefty loss sustained the previous day, when fears of a U.S. interest rate rise coupled with large option plays battered the market.

The AEX index of blue chip stocks ended the day 16.99 points, 2.39 percent, higher at 727.30. The market eased off its intra-day peak of 732.46 late in the session as a weaker early Wall Street and softer dollar sapped its strength.
The index plunged 24.73 points, 3.36 percent, on Thursday to 710.31, as markets interpreted comments from Fed chairman Alan Greenspan that the U.S. was more likely to raise interest rates.
But after a jittery start, Dutch stocks began climbing back this morning, with investor sentiment suported by a stronger dollar overnight and higher early bond markets.
Dealers said there were signs that the move on Thursday -- fuelled by panic options-related selling -- was over done and that there were bargains to be had.
"There was some relief that Wall Street didn't lose any more ground after we closed yesterday and it seems the institutional clients are back picking up stocks this morning," a dealer said.
However, with the option expiry looming in the afternoon the mood remained nervous and the recovery was slow to gather pace.

By the afternoon, all AEX stocks had moved to the positive, with index-sensitive financials leading the way. Banks ING and ABN AMRO both finished ahead, up 2.00 and 3.90 guilders at 71.10 and 126.70 respectively.
Insurer Aegon, which reported full-year 1996 earnings up 18.5 percent at 1.57 billion guilders, closed 2.60 up at 131.50.
It raised its dividend to 2.79 guilders from 2.37 and forecast a further rise in profits of 10 to 12 percent in 1997.
Philips' chairman Cor Boonstra told the company's annual shareholders meeting in Amsterdam it was still committed to double-digit profit growth over the next few years.
The news helped the shares finish 2.00 higher at 83.00.

Elsewhere, the dollar pushed up other stocks such as Royal Dutch, Unilever and Abhold, which have U.S. curency exposure, although some ended off their highs as the dollar eased. Royal Dutch closed 5.10 up at 332.10 and Ahold 7.80 firmer at 133.30.
But the jury remains out on whether Thursday's shake-out, one of the market's largest ever, was enough of a correction.

"The Dutch equity market is still not a bargain...If the FOMC decides to raise official rates by 50 basis points next week, the bottom will move a little more south," ING Barings said in a research note.
